pr_body:
This PR refactors the JsonSerializer metadata reading infrastructure with the following goals in mind:

1. Decouples it from the reference preservation feature for which it was tailor written. Support mixing and matching metadata properties from multiple features. Make it easier to add more metadata properties in the future.
2. Decouples the async metadata reading logic from the converter logic acting on the metadata. This is needed for polymorphism, where metadata must be consumed by derived converters.
3. Eliminates accidental complexity from the metadata reader implementation.

Additionally, this PR makes the following (closely related) changes:

* Implement metadata read support for the parameterized constructor converter. Relax restrictions when doing constructor deserialization with reference preservation enabled. Fix #66604.
* Fix reference handling in support in object deserialization. Implement reference handling support for `JsonUnknownTypeHandling.JsonNode`. Fix #67171.

Contributes to #63747.

issue_context.title: System.Text.Json ObjectConverter does not handle reference metadata correctly on deserialization
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-json See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
The following test fails with both `JsonElement` and `JsonNode` type handling. ```C# [Theory] [InlineData(JsonUnknownTypeHandling.JsonElement)] [InlineData(JsonUnknownTypeHandling.JsonNode)] public void ObjectConverterShouldHandleReferenceMetadata(JsonUnknownTypeHandling typehandling) { var options = new JsonSerializerOptions { ReferenceHandler = ReferenceHandler.Preserve, UnknownTypeHandling = typehandling }; string json = @"[{ ""$id"" : ""1"" },{ ""$ref"" : ""1""}]"; object[] deserialized = JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json, options); Assert.Same(deserialized[0], deserialized[1]); } ``` We need to update the `TryGetReferenceFromJsonElement` method in `ObjectConverter`: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f8d5706ab6e63b970a898ec293e04b47039abb70/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Converters/Object/ObjectConverter.cs#L43-L48 so that it handles both `$id` and `$ref` metadata. We also need to expose equivalent functionality for `JsonNode`, which currently is not implemented. cc @Jozkee @steveharter

Extracting any `$ref` metadata from the deserialized value should not be the responsibility of the converter. In any case, this logic is part of the ObjectConverter, it's not part of the deserialization hot path.
it still could be `WhateverClass.ReadValueOrReference(converter, ...)`

The changes in the JsonPath are due to the fact that reference metadata is passed to the ReferenceHandler at a later stage. This should have no noticeable impact on user experience, as the error message indicates that we read a nonexistent reference.
Seems reasonable. But this does make the path inconsistent with what the non-reference-handling would have produced, i.e. including the property name currently being deserialized. @Jozkee thoughts?

That discrepancy is intended. For example, if you deserialize a metadata property with invalid type, e.g.
```json
{ "$id" : false }
```
The error message will incorporate `$id` in the JsonPath. That's because the JSON violates System.Text.Json's metadata contract. On the other hand a JSON value such as
```json
{ "$id" : "badReferenceId", "$type" : "derivedClass", .... }
```
does not violate the metadata contract, but the string might get rejected by the reference resolver at a later stage by the DerivedClass converter. In this case, `$id` is not surfaced in the JsonPath (instead the existing error message clearly indicates that the `$id` value has been rejected by the resolver.

> The error message will incorporate $id in the JsonPath. That's because the JSON violates System.Text.Json's metadata contract.

I agree with this, those errors will always occur at the moment a metadata property is read and it feels natural to display $id, ref or other metadata in the exception path.

> does not violate the metadata contract, but the string might get rejected by the reference resolver at a later stage by the DerivedClass converter.

As long as the path is consistent, it should be fine IMO. Will the path always point to the parent on all cases where there are non-contract errors on metadata?

> Will the path always point to the parent on all cases where there are non-contract errors on metadata?

That's right.
could this be automatically happening on push/pop state rather than every converter
Nope, this code cannot be called invoked before the deserialized value has been constructed, which is a converter-specific operation.
should you be also removing `Id` flag here? I think you should create a routines for these so that these lines of code are consistent everywhere

Removing the flag is not necessary (since it's stored in the stack frame rather than the parent state object). I considered extracting to a method, however the logic is slightly different for objects and collections so it didn't provide a lot of benefit.
how (or why) is it different?

Well, fields defined in `ReadState` are unique in the deserialization context, whereas fields defined in `ReadStackFrame` are replicated for every value that is pushed in the stack -- there's no need to reset the latter kind.
